summary: Director John Landis illegally hired two young children for a night helicopter scene on the 1982 Twilight Zone movie; explosions downed the helicopter, killing them and actor Vic Morrow, and Landis was acquitted of manslaughter.

evidence.note: Landis biography begins with his 1950 birth in Chicago and move to Los Angeles
Warner Bros hires Landis and Spielberg for the Twilight Zone film in 1982
crew raise objections to using children at night near explosives; Landis rejects alternatives
producers hide the illegally employed children from the on-set fire safety officer
shoot takes place at Indian Dunes on the Santa Clara River in California
helicopter crashes, killing the two children and Vic Morrow
defense strategy blames below-the-line crew such as the pilot and pyrotechnicians
jury acquits Landis and co-defendants of manslaughter after a years-long case
brief coda on later career, Polanski petition and son Max Landis's abuse allegations

notes: Landis and the film are co-primary: the title names the film but the story is built around Landis. Considered partial_life (framed on one production) but the story gives a real biography from birth through his later career, so the lifetime rule applies; covered_span runs to release year as he is alive. Exorcist and Birds material is comparison background. George Folsey Jr. left out of subjects for uncertain dates.
